newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthens against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened against the dollar, boosted by inflows from agricultural exports and a lack of demand for dollars, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.46 against the dollar from 53.87 on Thursday while against the pound the shilling was posted at a commercial rate of 87.67 from 88.59.
"There is no demand (for dollars)," a bank dealer said.
There was some bargain-hunting but it appeared most players opted to wait until the shilling consolidated its gains against the dollar to buy at a cheaper rate, dealers said.
"The shilling is trying to find a new level. At the moment we're trading at 53.20/60," one dealer said.
Some dealers said a lot of people sold dollars to square their books ahead of the weekend after buying them from coffee and tea exporters Thursday afternoon .
The money market tightened marginally with the beginning of a new cash ratio period with several banks borrowing. Overnight rates were quoted at 20 percent from 16-18 percent on Thursday.
